title: Integral compactification of a separated etale chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $a:U\to X$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism with $U$ a scheme. There are an algebraic space $B$, an integral morphism $\pi:B\to X$, and a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow B$ such that $a=\pi\circ j$.

source.place: Tag 0ABS (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine), applied to a quasi-compact etale morphism; etale implies locally quasi-finite by morphisms.tex Tag 03WS (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite).

proof.text: For every scheme test $T\to X$, the pullback $U_T\to T$ is an etale scheme morphism by the hypothesis and [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It is unramified by the explicit conjunct in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to $U_T\to T$: it is quasi-finite at every point, including the finite-type neighbourhood condition in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Thus $a$ is locally quasi-finite on every scheme test and locally of finite type there. Together with the assumed quasi-compactness this makes $a$ of finite type, by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The morphism $a$ is representable by its etale hypothesis and is separated by assumption. These are exactly the hypotheses of the locus theorem used below.

source.place: Tag 0ABS, hypotheses; Tag 03XU (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite), via Morphisms Tags 03WS and 02V5. Here the item already assumes representability, so apply the scheme input on each test.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-integral-factorization] to the given quasi-compact separated map $a:U\to X$; it applies since for a quasi-compact scheme $T\to X$ the scheme $U_T$ is quasi-compact and its identity is the required etale atlas. Obtain $U\xrightarrow{j}B\xrightarrow{\pi}X$ with $\pi$ integral, $\pi\circ j=a$, and the universal property stated in [lem-sfb-space-normalization-quasifinite-locus]. By [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence] the integral morphism $\pi$ is separated: $\Delta_\pi:B\to B\times_XB$ is representable by closed immersions. Hence $\pi$ is quasi-separated in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation]: for an affine scheme $T\to B\times_XB$, the pullback $B\times_{B\times_XB}T$ is a closed subscheme of $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], homeomorphic to a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $|T|$, so quasi-compact. Now [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation], with $f=j$ and $g=\pi$, applies because $\pi\circ j=a$ is quasi-compact. It gives quasi-compactness of $j$ on affine tests, hence on every scheme test after covering it by affine opens. No global compactness, normality or Noetherian assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 0822 (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization); quasi-compactness of the first arrow is Tag 03KS with nu separated, as in the proof of 0ABS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-normalization-quasifinite-locus] to $a$ and the factorization of step 2, using representability, finite type and separatedness from step 1. It gives an open subspace $W\subseteq B$ for which $j^{-1}(W)$ is the quasi-finite locus of $a$, and $j^{-1}(W)\to W$ is an isomorphism. Every point is in that locus by step 1; consequently this open inverse image is all of $U$. Hence $j$ identifies $U$ with the open subspace $W$ of $B$ and is an open immersion. Its quasi-compactness, the integrality of $\pi$, and the equality $a=\pi\circ j$ were already supplied in step 2. This proves all clauses.

source.place: Tag 0ABS (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine), proof: apply 0ABR and use that the quasi-finite locus is the whole source.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0ABS, proof through 0ABR, with the normalization construction and quasi-compactness separated as supporting inputs.
